caption: Performance of different triggers. The words used as triggers on the horizontal axis are arranged in ascending order according to the ASR of the clean model.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the performance of different trigger words on the SST-2 dataset under dirty-label poisoning with 16 poisoned samples, measured by ASR (Attack Success Rate) on the vertical axis. The horizontal axis displays trigger words arranged in ascending order of the clean model’s ASR: "bb", "mb", "cf", "beautiful", "excellent", "gorgeous", "wonderful", "brilliant", and "beautifully". The x-axis is categorical with no numerical scale or units. The y-axis is numerical, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at 0.2 intervals, and is labeled "ASR". Three lines represent different trigger insertion strategies: "start" (green line with circle markers), "random" (orange line with cross markers), and "end" (purple line with circle markers). The "start" strategy begins at approximately 0.7 ASR for "bb", drops sharply to around 0.1 for "cf", then gradually increases to about 0.9 for "beautifully". The "random" strategy starts at approximately 0.1 for "bb", rises steadily to about 0.8 for "beautifully". The "end" strategy starts at approximately 0.4 for "bb", spikes to nearly 0.9 for "cf", then fluctuates before settling around 0.85 for "beautifully". All three lines show increasing trends toward the right end of the x-axis, with "start" and "end" achieving higher ASR values overall compared to "random" in the later trigger words.
